title: Ray McKinley's sound and a short job in his band
summary: Leeman admires McKinley's tuning and swing and recalls joining his band for five or six weeks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I mention Ray McKinley, a great drummer, whom I heard with the Dorsey brothers around '32 or '33. I heard him a couple of times in person on one nighters, and in Massachusetts and then back in my home town on the radio from Glen Island Casino -- I loved the sound of his drums, Ray McKinley. Here is tuning again -- his intense, but loose swinging beat and taste behind soloists. He's one of the masters of his time and through the years, a veteran swinger. He and I were also friends. I'm beginning to sound like Sammy Davis, but nevertheless, we were dear friends. I worked with his orchestra for a short while. When he hit the Fin egan book, and he asked me to go out on the road with him -- I went out for five or six weeks, and he said he'd split the book with me.

Well, it turned out that I did all the vocalists; Ray directed and did the vocalists, but when it came time to clear the swinging drum parts, Ray used to come back and say I've got it, Cliff. But however, he's a dear friend, and we shall remain that way.
